newsitem.title: USA: CME says developing Russia, China currency futures.
newsitem.headline: CME says developing Russia, China currency futures.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange is developing futures on Russian and Chinese currencies and may have them ready to launch "within a year," CME chairman Jack Sandner said Thursday.
"We're looking at Russia with the rouble," Sandner said at a news conference held for the launch of the CME's Mexican Cetes interest rate futures.

"When we mentioned the rouble and some of these other products, they're a ways off, but I wouldn't say a couple years," Sandner said. "I'm talking within a year -- the RMB (renminbi) in China, these kinds of products."
He said the launch of CME futures on the South African rand and New Zealand dollar was "four to five weeks away."
Rick Kilcollin, CME president and chief executive, said the exchange was also committed to other Latin American products.

"We've had a number of conversations in the last couple of years with Bovespa in Brazil about trading the Brazilian stock index markets," he said. "I think that's something that's still under discussion."

Sander said, "Our goal is to try to list the trilogy of products in the countries that are developing into a market -- the currency, the stock index and the fixed-income. We've done that now in Mexico, we'd like to do that in Brazil, we'd like to do that in Argentina, and probably the next country in South America would be Chile," he said.
The CME launched futures and options on 91-day Mexican Treasury bills, or Cetes, on Thursday. Trading in 28-day Mexican Equilibrium Interbank Interest Rate futures and options begins April 17.
